symbols.description: The two-year national legislative body in which House and Senate actions on bills occur.
symbols.name: Congress

symbols.description: One chamber of Congress, referred to as the House of Representatives.
symbols.name: House

symbols.description: One chamber of Congress.
symbols.name: Senate

symbols.description: A legislative chamber of Congress, specifically the House or Senate.
symbols.name: Chamber

symbols.description: A leader of a party in a congressional chamber who plans and coordinates congressional action on bills.
symbols.name: Party leader

symbols.description: A leader of the majority party in the House or Senate who has roles in setting the agenda or bringing bills to the floor.
symbols.name: Majority party leader

symbols.description: A proposed legislative measure introduced by a Member of the House or Senate and potentially considered by committees and a chamber.
symbols.name: Bill

symbols.description: A panel of Members that holds policy expertise and typically leads in developing and assessing proposed legislation within a specified policy jurisdiction.
symbols.name: Standing committee

symbols.description: A congressional body that may receive referred bills, conduct hearings and markups, and report bills to its chamber.
symbols.name: Committee

symbols.description: The specified policy area or areas over which a committee has authority regarding elements of a bill.
symbols.name: Committee jurisdiction

symbols.description: A Member of the House or Senate who may introduce a bill or participate in committee action.
symbols.name: Member

symbols.description: The chair of a committee who has primary authority to set the committee agenda and identify bills for formal committee attention.
symbols.name: Committee chair

symbols.description: The primary authority of a committee chair to determine which bills receive formal committee attention.
symbols.name: Committee agenda-setting authority

symbols.description: Action undertaken to develop, assess, or advance legislation, including action initiated by a committee.
symbols.name: Legislative action

symbols.description: The process by which an introduced bill is referred to the committee or committees with jurisdiction over its elements.
symbols.name: Bill referral

symbols.description: A committee's formal consideration of a referred bill during the Congress.
symbols.name: Formal committee consideration

symbols.description: Legislative action initiated by a committee rather than limited to bills referred to it.
symbols.name: Committee-initiated legislative action

symbols.description: A committee event providing committee members and the public an opportunity to hear selected parties discuss a bill's strengths and weaknesses.
symbols.name: Hearing

symbols.description: A Member participating in the work of a committee, including hearing and markup activities.
symbols.name: Committee member

symbols.description: The public audience given an opportunity at a hearing to hear selected parties discuss a bill.
symbols.name: Public

symbols.description: A party invited to provide views at a committee hearing about a bill's strengths and weaknesses.
symbols.name: Selected party

symbols.description: An example of a selected party that may provide views at a committee hearing.
symbols.name: Federal agency

symbols.description: An example of a selected party that may provide views at a committee hearing.
symbols.name: Organized interest

symbols.description: The strengths and weaknesses of a bill discussed at a committee hearing.
symbols.name: Bill strengths and weaknesses

symbols.description: A committee proceeding during which committee members vote on proposed amendments to a bill.
symbols.name: Markup

symbols.description: A proposed change to a bill considered and voted on by committee members during a markup.
symbols.name: Proposed amendment

symbols.description: The vote by which a committee agrees to report a bill, and the voting threshold applied to proposed amendments in a markup.
symbols.name: Majority vote

symbols.description: A committee's formal recommendation that its parent chamber consider a bill, including any changes adopted in the markup.
symbols.name: Bill report

symbols.description: The House or Senate to which a committee reports a bill for consideration.
symbols.name: Parent chamber

symbols.description: Consideration of a bill by the full House or Senate on the chamber floor.
symbols.name: Floor consideration

symbols.description: A majority party leader in the House who generally decides which bills receive floor consideration and may schedule them or seek tailored parameters.
symbols.name: House majority party leader

symbols.description: A type of floor consideration for which House majority party leaders may schedule a bill.
symbols.name: Streamlined floor consideration

symbols.description: The committee that House majority party leaders may ask to propose tailored parameters for a bill's floor consideration.
symbols.name: Rules Committee

symbols.description: A set of parameters proposed for the House floor consideration of a bill.
symbols.name: Tailored floor-consideration parameters

symbols.description: A motion in the Senate to proceed to a specific bill, typically offered by the majority leader.
symbols.name: Senate motion to proceed

symbols.description: The majority leader who typically offers a Senate motion to proceed to a specific bill.
symbols.name: Senate majority leader

symbols.description: A Member of the Senate who may object to a unanimous consent request to bring a bill to the floor.
symbols.name: Senator

symbols.description: A request in the Senate to bring a specific bill to the floor, effective if no Senator objects.
symbols.name: Unanimous consent request

symbols.description: A Senator's objection to a unanimous consent request to bring a bill to the Senate floor.
symbols.name: Objection
